newsitem.title: USA: More U.S.-Kurdish talks in Ankara next week.
newsitem.headline: More U.S.-Kurdish talks in Ankara next week.

text.p: A senior U.S. official who held talks with the two rival Iraqi Kurdish factions in Washington this week will meet them again in Ankara next week, the State Department said on Friday.

Spokesman Nicholas Burns gave no precise date for the follow-up meeting between Assistant Secretary of State Robert Pelletreau and delegations of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK).

Burns said Thursday's talks at the State Department "were part of our effort to consolidate the ceasefire in north Iraq and to try to promote some kind of reconciliation among the population of north Iraq".
Neither KDP leader Massoud Barzani nor PUK leader Jalal Talabani took part in the Washington talks and Burns said he did not know if they would join the Ankara discussions.

A KDP decision last August to invite Iraqi troops into the Western-protected Kurdish region to help oust the PUK from the city of Arbil sparked two months of fighting between the two factions, ended by a U.S.-brokered ceasefire.

The increased influence this gave Baghdad in the region forced an end to the Western military presence there. Washington also evacuated more than 6,000 Kurds and Iraqis it feared could be at risk from Iraqi President Saddam Hussein.
Although no major fighting has occurred since October, the two groups remain divided over oil trade revenues on the Turkish border and the status of Arbil.
